tokens.source: dispatch 4 (this one) is the completion attempt; prior dispatches cost 922,329 tokens across three attempts (219,085 fit-analysis + 313,244 chip-scale build + ~390,000 spine-fold build), so the CUMULATIVE cost of FFT64Block spans four dispatches

notes: DISPATCH 4 (2026-08-24) - COMPLETED. Entered with the block placing, routing, building and executing all 84 cells but emitting only the FIRST sample's word, root-caused by the previous dispatch to an INV-33 state/instruction OVERLAP in two cells. That diagnosis was correct and a THIRD instance was found by the gate written for it. HOW THE WORDS WERE FREED, and the proof the arithmetic is unchanged: mcalc gave up a dead 'BR.Z +0' pad (the conditional negate only ever needs to skip the negate itself - on the not-taken path R0 already holds r-M >= 0, which IS |r-M|) and a 'CMP t, zero' that re-derived a Z flag the preceding 'SUB mconst, t' had already set (the only instruction between them is a MOVE, and MOVE does not touch flags); fetch_d and tab_d moved their forwarded word to the INV-33 ACCUMULATOR-DELIVERY idiom, where it arrives in R0 and the cell's FIRST instruction re-emits it before any ALU op can disturb R0, freeing both the input register and the staging MOVE. Every reduced cell was then run on a REAL simKYT cell against the UNREDUCED program over its whole input domain (mcalc: every (r,o) at both N, 192 pairs; fetch: every direct-table shape of FFT64 and FFT16 over 3 full pointer cycles, 290 triggers; tab: every (m,k) incl. both trivial encodings, 288 triggers) - zero mismatches. The three pre-fix shapes cannot be resolved at all (33 words), which IS the defect. APPROACHES REJECTED, and why: re-expressing fetch_d's pointer wrap to drop a constant (masking needs the table 16-ALIGNED, and addresses 0/1 are R0 and the input, so no aligned base exists; deriving pbase from pend costs 2 instructions to save 1 word, net zero; ADC against the always-zero R31 needs a carry that is not reliably set across triggers); exploiting the d-table's palindrome (a real fold, but the triangle index costs more than the 1 word it saves); moving the c forward into fetch_c (would have worked, but it makes fetch_c's last-listed edge a NON-successor and risks the route-time face rule and the 349-edge hop audit for no gain over R0 delivery); splitting fetch_d into two cells (safe but changes the cell count and the stage's chain PARITY, cascading into the spine plan). THEN THE SECOND DEFECT, which the overlap fix exposed: with the block streaming, a 100-sample run diverged from output 95 by a constant (+87,-87), deterministic across two runs and reproduced identically with the tab_d reduction reverted (so not a regression). Exhaustive fault searches - every single wrong twiddle word in every stage, every slot substitution/rotation/pointer stall, every ring-timing offset (phase -3..+3 x depth -1..+1), every free-running slot offset - ALL failed to reproduce it. What found it was instrumentation, not modelling: an IMPULSE stimulus (which makes the ideal output constant, so a phase error reads as a rotation: all 32 odd-bin slots came out 512*W64^1 = (510,-50) instead of (512,0)), then reading the steer cell's latched (csav,dsav) off the running chip trigger by trigger. Wrong at exactly triggers 0 and 16 - the two TRIVIAL slots - and correct at all 30 others. Cause: swap had ONE jump port wired to sign's `num` entry, leaving sign's `triv` entry DEAD CODE. Promoted to INV-35. It had hidden because the standalone fold-chain check drove sign's entries BY HAND from the control word, exercising code the built chip could not reach - that harness now reads the decision OFF the cell and asserts it agrees with the control word. AFTER THE FIX: impulse 0/260 mismatches and random 260/260 bit-exact on chip. COST NOTE: this dispatch also corrected its OWN premature claim - an 80-sample run was reported bit-exact before the reach arithmetic showed it never touches the twiddled half; the correction is in the commit history rather than quietly amended. TWO MORE DEFECTS FOUND BY THE FINAL FULL-SUITE RUN, both TEST-SIDE and both corrected in the commit history rather than quietly amended. (a) The saturated gate reported a LIVELOCK. It was not one: the harness's default budget is 2000 events/sample, sized for small blocks, while FFT64 MEASURES 2873 events/sample on chip (8 consecutive samples, range 2727..2969), so a 127-sample burst needs ~365k events against a 254k cap and expired mid-burst. Re-run with a real budget the identical burst completes BIT-EXACT, 254/254 words, at 6000 and again at 40000 events/sample - all six stage serialize-LOCKs do release under back-to-back drive. The gate now pins the MEASURED per-sample cost as a named constant and uses 2x it as a CEILING on a bounded run, so a genuine livelock (which never reaches quiescence at ANY budget) is still caught; a cap enlarged until green would have been a loosened tolerance wearing a different hat. The harness message was also fixed - it said 'block livelocks when the pipeline is full', naming a CONCLUSION it cannot distinguish from a budget shortfall, and that cost a commit asserting a defect that did not exist. (b) WORSE: the report writer emitted "passed": true UNCONDITIONALLY, so the failing run still produced a GREEN report the dashboard would have believed. Fixed so it cannot recur - the report file is unlinked at the start of the writer (absence is the safe state, read as 'not verified'), and the write happens only when pytest's own terminalreporter shows zero failures; proven by running the writer in a session containing a synthetic failing test and asserting it refuses, fails, and leaves no file. FINAL RESULT: 45/45 green in 59s, report written by a genuinely all-green session. MERGE NOTE (FFT32 landed in parallel and touched the same file): FFT32Block independently hit the SAME s1_fetch_d overlap at N=32's P=16 boundary and fixed it by REMOVING the c-word cross-forward entirely, so each table cell writes straight into steer's own input register. That shape leaves the cell at 30/32 words - two clear - where this dispatch's accumulator-delivery fix left 31/32, so the merge KEEPS FFT32's version and drops this one: there is ONE _fetch_cell and no divergence between sizes. The mcalc fix here (dead BR.Z pad + redundant CMP) is unaffected and still required - N=32 has no octant fold, so it never reached that cell. Both planner improvements survive and are complementary: FFT32's _face_rule_ok (the route-time face rule as a placement CONSTRAINT rather than an after-the-fact audit) and this dispatch's five corridor-check corrections, height-capped fallback, and declared-anchor contract.
